summary: This document defines an XML format for describing filters on SIP event notifications. A subscriber can use it to say which state changes of a resource should trigger notifications and what those notifications should contain.

eli5.summary: This is the form you fill in to tell a notification service what to tell you about. It is written in a tidy computer format that both sides can read.

questions: what is a sip simple-filter document
how do sip notification filters work
what do include and exclude do in sip filters
subtitle: An XML format that lets a SIP subscriber say which changes to a resource it wants to hear about, and what to include.

tldr.problem: SIP event notification lets a subscriber learn of state changes to a resource, but it has no way to say which changes matter or which parts of the state to deliver. That is costly for devices with low bandwidth and limited battery.
tldr.mechanism: A simple-filter document in XML has a what part that selects content with XPath-like expressions and trigger parts that say which changes (changed, added, removed) cause a notification.
tldr.outcome: Subscribers can cut notifications down to what they need. The format is extensible by new namespaces and registers the media type application/simple-filter+xml.

today: RFC 4661 is a Proposed Standard from September 2006. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is paired with RFC 4660, which describes the filtering function.

sections.title: Why Filter Notifications
sections.content:
The SIP event notification framework (RFC 3265) lets a subscriber ask to be told when the state of a resource changes. It has no mechanism for filtering: stating which notification content is wanted and when it should be sent.

This RFC supplies a format for that, an XML document. It holds the user's preferences for when notifications go out (triggering) and what they contain. The RFC expects it to help most with mobile wireless devices, which typically have high latency, low bandwidth, low processing power, small displays and limited battery. It also warns implementers about the computational burden filtering puts on the source of the notifications. The functional description of filtering is in RFC 4660.
sections.eli5: Without a filter, a news service texts you every headline. A filter lets you say only tell me about football, and only when the score changes.

sections.title: The Filter Document Structure
sections.content:
A simple-filter is an XML 1.0 document, encoded in UTF-8, that MUST be well formed and valid against the applicable schemas. Its namespace is urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:simple-filter and its media type is application/simple-filter+xml.

The root element is <filter-set>. It has an optional package attribute naming the event package it applies to, may contain one <ns-bindings> element, and contains one or more <filter> elements. Each <ns-binding> maps a prefix to a namespace urn for use in expressions.

A <filter> has a required id that MUST be unique in the set. It may have a uri for one resource (useful with event lists) or a domain for resources in a domain, but never both. A filter can be removed with remove, or switched off and on with enabled (default true). A new filter MUST contain a <what> or a <trigger>. Changing a filter means resending it with the same id.
sections.eli5: The filter is a form with a title, a list of what the words mean, and one or more rules. Each rule has its own name tag so you can change or turn it off later.

sections.title: Choosing Content with the what Element
sections.content:
The <what> element gives rules for building the content to deliver. It holds <include> and <exclude> elements. Includes are additive: each adds an element or attribute to the resulting XML document. Each exclude removes content from it.

Both elements take a type attribute. xpath (the default) selects an element or attribute with the restricted XPath-like syntax. namespace takes a namespace URI and selects all elements defined in it.

The result MUST stay valid against its schema. Mandatory elements are added automatically, and an optional element is kept if one of its attributes is selected. If an exclude would make the document invalid, that step MUST be reversed. So a subscriber normally only includes or excludes optional items, and SHOULD NOT exclude mandatory ones.

Selecting /presence/tuple/status/basic also brings along its ancestors, <status> and <tuple>.
sections.eli5: Include is a highlighter pen for the parts you want, and exclude is a black marker for the parts you do not. The page still has to make sense when you are done.

sections.title: Deciding When with the trigger Element
sections.content:
A <trigger> names a package-specific change a resource must undergo before content is delivered. Several <trigger> elements in one filter are an OR. Inside one trigger, the <changed>, <added> and <removed> elements are an AND, and at least one of them MUST be present.

  • <changed> fires when the value of an element or attribute differs from the previous document, meaning the raw version of the last document sent before filters were applied. Optional from, to and by attributes narrow it. Rewriting the same value is not a change.
  • <added> fires when an element appears that was not in the previous document.
  • <removed> fires when an element that was in the previous document is gone.

The by attribute is numeric. With by set to 2 and a current value of 6, the trigger fires when the value reaches 8 or more, or falls to 4 or less. If by is combined with from or to, those must be of type decimal.
sections.eli5: Triggers are like alarm rules: ring when the door opens, ring when a new toy shows up, or ring when the temperature moves by two degrees.

sections.title: The Expression Syntax
sections.content:
Selections use an ABNF-defined syntax that is XPath compatible but only a restricted subset of it. A selection is a reference optionally followed by a bracketed condition. References can use a full path such as /presence/tuple/status/basic, any level with //tuple/status/basic, or a star wildcard. Conditions compare with =, < or > and join with and or or.

If an expression matches more than one element, all of them are selected. Namespace prefixes are expanded through <ns-bindings>, following XPath 1.0 rules. When the document uses a default namespace, an <ns-binding> SHOULD define an equal URI under a prefix so evaluation works.
sections.eli5: It is a tiny addressing language for pointing at one spot in a big document, like saying second shelf, third book, where the cover is red.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives six examples built on presence data. One selects only the <basic> status of tuples whose class is IM, SMS or MMS. Another fires when a status changes from CLOSED to OPEN and then delivers the full presence state. A third combines <what> and <trigger> to report watchers whose status becomes pending or waiting.

Others select everything in the PIDF namespace, pick a game-specific tuple, or use two filters on different resources, one of which excludes the PIDF <note> element.
sections.eli5: The examples show real forms: tell me when my friend comes online, or only show me who is waiting for my approval.

sections.title: Extensibility, Security and IANA
sections.content:
The format is meant to be extended by defining new elements in a new namespace with a new schema. Extensions MUST NOT change the syntax or meaning of this schema, and receivers MUST be able to ignore them safely. The schema marks where extensions may go with any and anyAttribute, and it carries no version number.

Filters strongly affect how a server handles a request, so messages carrying them should be authenticated and authorised. Digest Authentication from RFC 3261 is named as one way. Requests can reveal a user agent's capabilities, so sensitive ones SHOULD be encrypted with SIP S/MIME. The filtering security measures of RFC 3265 MUST be followed along with package-specific security.

IANA registers the media type application/simple-filter+xml, the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:simple-filter and the schema.
sections.eli5: Other people can add new boxes to the form, but they cannot change what the old boxes mean. And since the form controls what a server does, the server should check who is asking.

data.title: Notify when a contact becomes available
data.code:
<filter-set xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:simple-filter">
  <ns-bindings>
    <ns-binding prefix="pidf" urn="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf"/>
  </ns-bindings>
  <filter id="123" uri="sip:presentity@example.com">
    <trigger>
      <changed from="CLOSED" to="OPEN">
        /pidf:presence/pidf:tuple/pidf:status/pidf:basic
      </changed>
    </trigger>
  </filter>
</filter-set>
